title: Structure and Properties of Matter
seo_title: Grade 12 Chemistry (SCH4U): Structure and Properties of Matter Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: The development of the atomic model; the quantum mechanical model, quantum numbers and orbitals; electron configurations; VSEPR theory and molecular shapes; hybridization; polarity, intermolecular forces and the properties of ionic, molecular, covalent network and metallic solids. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Chemistry, Grade 12, University Preparation (SCH4U), Strand C: Structure and Properties of Matter)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Chemistry (SCH4U) worksheets on the structure of matter: the quantum mechanical model, quantum numbers, electron configurations, VSEPR shapes, hybridization, polarity and types of solids. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Electrons fill orbitals in order of energy: 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d.
key_sub: VSEPR: electron pairs spread out as far as possible.
body_html:
How to think about it

The quantum mechanical model describes electrons by four quantum numbers (n, l, ml, ms). Orbitals fill from lowest energy (aufbau principle), each holds two electrons of opposite spin (Pauli), and electrons spread out singly before pairing (Hund).

VSEPR theory predicts shape from the number of bonding and lone pairs around the central atom: 4 bonding pairs give a tetrahedral shape (109.5°), 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair a trigonal pyramidal shape (107°), 2 bonding and 2 lone pairs a bent shape (104.5°). A molecule with polar bonds is polar only if the dipoles do not cancel.

Example

Electron configuration of sulfur (Z = 16)?

Fill 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p

Answer: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴

Example

Shape of NH₃?

3 bonding pairs, 1 lone pair

Answer: trigonal pyramidal

Common mistakes

  • Filling 3d before 4s.
  • Calling CO₂ polar because its bonds are polar: the linear shape cancels the dipoles.
  • Forgetting lone pairs when choosing a molecular shape.

faq.a: Every atom is held by strong covalent bonds in a giant structure.

items.q: Calculate the energy, in eV, of a photon of wavelength 260 nm.
What is the energy of the electron in the n = 3 orbit of He⁺? (E<sub>n</sub> = −13.6 Z²/n² eV)
Which quantum number gives the shape of an orbital?
items.e: l = 0 is spherical (s), l = 1 dumb-bell (p).

items.q: Calculate the frequency of light of wavelength 500 nm.
What is the radius of the n = 2 orbit in He⁺? (r = 52.9 n²/Z pm)
What does the Heisenberg uncertainty principle say?
c: the exact position and momentum of an electron cannot both be known
items.e: Δx × Δp ≥ h/4π.

items.q: Calculate the energy of a photon of wavelength 440 nm.
Calculate the frequency of light of wavelength 310 nm.
Calculate the energy of a photon of wavelength 710 nm.
How many orbitals are there altogether in the shell with n = 3?
items.e: Number of orbitals = n² = 9.

items.q: Electrons are accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 100 V. Calculate their de Broglie wavelength.
items.e: ½mv² = eV gives v = 5.93 × 106 m/s. λ = h/(mv) = 1.23 × 10−10 m.

items.q: Calculate the specific charge of the nucleus <sup>60</sup><sub>27</sub>Co. Take the mass of a nucleon as 1.67 × 10<sup>−27</sup> kg.
items.e: Specific charge = charge ÷ mass = (27 × 1.60 × 10−19) ÷ (60 × 1.67 × 10−27) = 4.31 × 107 C/kg.

items.q: What is the energy of the electron in the n = 6 orbit of a hydrogen atom? (E<sub>n</sub> = −13.6/n² eV)
How many orbitals are there altogether in the shell with n = 5?
items.e: Number of orbitals = n² = 25.

items.q: How many neutrons are in the nucleus <sup>235</sup><sub>92</sub>U?
items.e: Neutrons = nucleon number − proton number = 235 − 92 = 143.

items.q: What is the energy of the electron in the n = 2 orbit of Li²⁺? (E<sub>n</sub> = −13.6 Z²/n² eV)
Calculate the energy, in eV, of a photon of wavelength 740 nm.
What is the electron configuration of Ti<sup>3+</sup>?
items.e: Transition metals lose their 4s electrons first, then 3d. Ti is [Ar] 3d² 4s².

items.q: How many neutrons are in the nucleus <sup>60</sup><sub>27</sub>Co?
items.e: Neutrons = nucleon number − proton number = 60 − 27 = 33.

items.q: What are the allowed values of m<sub>l</sub> for a 4f electron?
items.e: m<sub>l</sub> runs from −l to +l.

items.q: A mass spectrum of a sample of iridium shows 191 with abundance 75.0% and 193 with abundance 25.0%. Calculate the relative atomic mass.
How many unpaired electrons are there in a free V²⁺ ion (high spin)?
items.e: Its d configuration gives 3 unpaired electrons.

items.q: How many unpaired electrons are there in a free V³⁺ ion (high spin)?
items.e: Its d configuration gives 2 unpaired electrons.

items.q: A mass spectrum of a sample of rubidium shows 85 with abundance 30.0% and 87 with abundance 70.0%. Calculate the relative atomic mass.
Why do Zr and Hf have almost the same radius?
c: they are in the same period
items.e: So they are hard to separate.

items.q: Why are transition metal compounds often coloured?
items.e: The colour seen is the complementary colour.

items.q: How many electrons are in p orbitals altogether in an atom of Mn (Z = 25)?
items.e: Configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁵ 4s²: add every p sub-shell to get 12.

items.q: What is the electron configuration of Cu<sup>2+</sup>?
items.e: Transition metals lose their 4s electrons first, then 3d. Cu is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹.

items.q: How many unpaired electrons are there in a free Cr³⁺ ion (high spin)?
items.e: Its d configuration gives 3 unpaired electrons.

items.q: A mass spectrum of chlorine shows 35 with abundance 75.8% and 37 with abundance 24.2%. Calculate the relative atomic mass.
How many unpaired electrons are there in a free Mn²⁺ ion (high spin)?
items.e: Its d configuration gives 5 unpaired electrons.

items.e: Configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁸ 4s²: add every p sub-shell to get 12.

items.e: Its d configuration gives 4 unpaired electrons.

items.e: Transition metals lose their 4s electrons first, then 3d. Fe is [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s².

How many unpaired electrons are there in a free Fe³⁺ ion (high spin)?
items.e: Its d configuration gives 5 unpaired electrons.

items.q: What is the shape of NH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>?
items.e: 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs around the central atom: bent (non-linear).

items.q: Why is the bond angle in water (104.5°) less than in methane (109.5°)?
c: two lone pairs on oxygen push the bonds closer
items.e: Lone pairs repel more strongly.

items.q: What is the shape of PCl₅?
items.e: PCl₅: trigonal bipyramidal.

items.q: What is the hybridization of carbon in C₂H₂?
items.e: C₂H₂: sp.

items.q: What is the shape of BeCl<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: 2 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs around the central atom: linear.

items.q: Which molecule has an expanded octet?
items.e: Phosphorus has ten electrons around it.

items.q: What is the bond angle in NH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>?
items.e: 2 bonding pairs, 2 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: What is the shape of CCl<sub>4</sub>?
items.e: 4 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs around the central atom: tetrahedral.

items.q: How many lone pairs of electrons are on the central atom in SF<sub>4</sub>?
items.e: SF4: 4 bonding pairs and 1 lone pairs.

items.q: What is the bond angle in NH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: 3 bonding pairs, 1 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: What is the shape of NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup>?
items.e: 4 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs around the central atom: tetrahedral.

items.q: What is the shape of H<sub>2</sub>O?
items.e: 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs around the central atom: bent (non-linear).

items.q: What is the shape of CO<sub>2</sub>?

items.e: PCl₅: sp³d hybridized, trigonal bipyramidal.

items.q: What is the hybridization of the central atom in C₂H₂ (each carbon)?
items.e: C₂H₂ (each carbon): sp hybridized, linear.

items.q: What is the bond angle in H<sub>2</sub>O?
items.e: 2 bonding pairs, 2 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: What is the hybridization of the central atom in NH₃ (nitrogen)?

items.q: Which of these has a sp³-hybridized central atom?
items.e: H₂O (oxygen): sp³ hybridized, bent (V-shaped).

items.q: Using molecular orbital theory, what is the bond order of He₂⁺?
items.e: Bond order = ½(Nb − Na) for 3 electrons = ½.

items.q: What is the bond angle in XeF<sub>4</sub>?
items.e: 4 bonding pairs, 2 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: Using molecular orbital theory, what is the bond order of Li₂?
items.e: Bond order = ½(Nb − Na) for 6 electrons = 1.

items.q: What is the bond angle in H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>?

items.q: Which of these has a sp-hybridized central atom?

items.q: Using molecular orbital theory, what is the bond order of O₂²⁻?

items.q: What is the bond angle in CCl<sub>4</sub>?

items.q: What is the bond angle in PH<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: 3 bonding pairs, 1 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: How many pairs of electrons are shared in a molecule of ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>)?
items.e: Ammonia has three single covalent bonds: 3 shared pairs.

items.q: Why does magnesium have a higher melting point than sodium?
c: Mg²⁺ has a larger charge and there are more delocalized electrons
items.e: Stronger metallic bonding.

items.q: Why is an alloy harder than the pure metal?
c: Atoms of different sizes disrupt the regular layers, so the layers cannot slide easily.
items.e: Properties depend on the particles and the forces between them.

items.q: Why is diamond very hard?
c: Each carbon atom is joined to four others by strong covalent bonds in a giant 3D structure.
It has weak forces between layers.
items.e: Properties depend on the particles and the forces between them.

items.q: What type of covalent bonding is in a molecule of methane (CH<sub>4</sub>)?
items.e: Count the shared pairs in the dot-and-cross diagram.

items.q: Why is graphite soft and used as a lubricant?
c: Its layers are held by weak forces and can slide over each other.
items.e: Properties depend on the particles and the forces between them.

items.q: Why are metals malleable?
c: Layers of positive ions can slide over each other without breaking the metallic bonding.
items.e: Properties depend on the particles and the forces between them.

items.q: Why does molten sodium chloride conduct electricity?
c: Its ions are free to move and carry charge.
items.e: Properties depend on the particles and the forces between them.

items.q: A nonstick pan coating repels water and oil. Which explanation at the molecular level is best?
c: Its polymer is covered in fluorine atoms that attract other molecules very weakly.
Each soap molecule has a water-loving end and a grease-loving end.
Its long, straight chains are held side by side by many hydrogen bonds.
Long, tangled polymer chains straighten when pulled and coil again.
items.e: Structure explains the property.

items.q: How many pairs of electrons are shared in a molecule of nitrogen (N<sub>2</sub>)?
items.e: Nitrogen has triple covalent bonds: 3 shared pairs.

items.q: Graphite is slippery and used in pencils. Which explanation at the molecular level is best?
c: In graphite each carbon has one electron free to move along the layers.
Carbon atoms form flat layers that slide over each other.
Each carbon atom is covalently bonded to four others in a rigid 3D network.
It is mostly tiny pores of air held in a network of silicon and oxygen.
items.e: Structure explains the property.

items.q: Which property is explained by this structure: “Its polymer is covered in fluorine atoms that attract other molecules very weakly.”
c: A nonstick pan coating repels water and oil
Table salt shatters when hit with a hammer
Silica aerogel is a very good insulator
Kevlar in body armour is very strong
items.e: Match structure to function.

items.q: What is the strongest type of intermolecular force?
items.e: Covalent bonds are within molecules, not between them.

items.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity?
c: its layers are held by covalent bonds
it has delocalized electrons between the layers
items.e: Each carbon uses three electrons in bonds; the fourth is delocalized.

items.q: Which change makes a molecule's van der Waals forces stronger?
c: a longer chain with more electrons
items.e: Straight long chains have more surface contact.

items.q: What is the bond angle in NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup>?
items.e: 4 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2.5°.

items.q: What type of covalent bonding is in a molecule of nitrogen (N<sub>2</sub>)?
items.e: Count the shared pairs in the dot-and-cross diagram.

items.q: What type of covalent bonding is in a molecule of ammonia (NH<sub>3</sub>)?
items.e: Count the shared pairs in the dot-and-cross diagram.

items.q: Which molecule is polar?
items.e: CO₂, CCl₄ and BF₃ are symmetrical, so the dipoles cancel.

items.q: Soap removes grease from your hands. Which explanation at the molecular level is best?
c: Each carbon atom is covalently bonded to four others in a rigid 3D network.
It is mostly tiny pores of air held in a network of silicon and oxygen.
Each soap molecule has a water-loving end and a grease-loving end.
Shifting the ions lines up like charges, which repel.
items.e: Structure explains the property.
